extracted.intended_audience: ship captains and officers of an exploratory fleet (early 17th-century Spanish voyage)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of orders and standards for discipline, navigation, provisioning, lookout, signals, dealings with natives, and emergency procedures to be followed by captains and officers during a long exploratory voyage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Christian, political, and military discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Admiral is specially charged to maintain Christian, political, and military discipline among the men of his ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General injunction to keep order and discipline aboard; the following specific prohibitions and punishments are corollaries of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid blasphemy and profane speech (punishments specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent cursing, blasphemy, or speaking evil against God, the Virgin, angels, saints, or sacred things; punish offenders severely and rigorously as their crimes deserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offender forfeits his ration for that day (or next day if already taken); first offence may be pardoned, but second/third may result in irons or a fine for the benefit of souls in purgatory; a copy of this chapter is to be nailed to the ship's main mast so all know the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit gambling (cards/dice) with narrow exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not consent to any playings with dice or cards for any stakes; dice/cards (except for backgammon) are to be thrown overboard if found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If table games cause disputes and trouble they are to be thrown overboard to avoid occasions for mischief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily communal devotion (Litany of Our Lady of Loreto)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every day in the afternoon all the people must go on their knees before an altar with images of Christ and the Virgin and recite the Litany of Our Lady of Loreto, praying for guidance and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as both a religious duty and practical petition for success of the voyage; intended to be performed daily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid disrespectful words about the monarch or service
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant to prevent free or disrespectful words about the royal person or his service; offenders to be punished promptly and with rigour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment should be justified and proportionate; an element of maintaining political loyalty and order aboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kind and firm treatment of crew; respect for officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat people kindly and lovingly, honour and maintain each officer in their post, cause them to be respected and to respect each other; govern so crew are contented, truthful, faithful, and loyal without harshness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised as the mark of a worthy Captain: governing in peace 'without the use of knife or other rigour.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Master to prevent provisions spoilage and manage use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master of the Ship must ensure provisions do not turn bad or get wasted, and items suspected of going bad are to be used first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close supervision of stores to prevent waste and ensure ship health and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily ration specification and rationing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily ration per person: 1½ lbs biscuit, 1 lb meat, 2 oz bacon, 1 oz pulses, half a gallon of water for drinking, and sufficient for cooking; fish days: one fish (or part if large), 6 oz pulses, measure of oil and vinegar, biscuit and water as on meat days; if no fish, substitute 4 oz cheese.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extras to be handled sensibly to avoid complaints; rations may be reduced in emergencies (example later: water reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow prescribed navigational courses and search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Capitana's course (e.g., W.S.W. until latitude 30°; alter to N.W. to latitude 10°15′; on that parallel steer west in search of specific islands; procedures for anchoring in a named port and waiting three months for other ships; if alone, raise cross and bury narrative jar, then continue specified route to New Guinea and Manila).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit step-by-step routing and contingency plans in case of separation; arrival procedures (anchor, wait, raise cross/bury record) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record celestial observations and correct for leeway/variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the sun daily and at night the star Crucero (or other known stars) whenever weather admits; know latitude and plot on chart, make allowances for lee-way, winds, currents, and variation of the needle; correct by sun or known meridian star for accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For greater accuracy, take multiple observations and note corrections explicitly in the log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep detailed daily log and charting of places and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Note number of leagues made each day, winds and changes, showers, currents, flights of birds, shoals of fishes, signs of land, islands (inhabited/uninhabited) and place them on chart with latitude, longitude, and form; for continental land note ports, capes, anchorages, rivers, wood and water locations, rocks, reefs, and describe positions and features. Denote sandy bottom by dots of ink, rocks by small crosses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also record colour, shape, dress of inhabitants, food, arms, boats, behaviour, government and religion so a full report can be given to the King.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and salute the Capitana; seek the word
rubrics_metrics.description: Every day come up to the Capitana to give respects and wish a good voyage; ask for 'the word' which will be answered in the customary way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains chain of command and communication rituals between ships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous lookout and watchkeeping (masthead & sentries)
rubrics_metrics.description: At sunrise and sunset, and oftener if desirable, two men go to the masthead to look out; at night sentries are to be doubled (one on bowsprit); the Admiral must make rounds and over-rounds in person or delegate to trusted officers and punish those negligent or sleeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuality and personal oversight are required; in taking in sail during threatening weather there must be no negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized signals for manoeuvre and distress
rubrics_metrics.description: When Capitana puts out a flag from main topmast, pilots must close; if Capitana alters course at night fire a gun; two guns signify land sighted or rocks; repeat signals to confirm understanding. By day show a flag on main rigging to communicate; by night show two lights besides stern lantern to signal help needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All ships must echo signals (repeat) so that understanding is confirmed; day/night procedures specified for various needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict fire precautions between decks
rubrics_metrics.description: No lighted candle or other fire between decks except within a lantern under charge of a trustworthy watchman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty of lantern watch should only be given to someone who can be trusted; fire prevention is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent fraud and waste of royal stores (cord, powder, balls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take much care that there is no waste in cord, powder, or balls; attend to all royal stores to prevent any fraud in their expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close accountability of military and royal supplies is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to sudden calms/odd sea behaviour by heaving to and sounding
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is both wind and sea and both suddenly cease at night, heave to and sound and keep a good lookout: the cause may be nearby land. Similarly if puffs/flaws or the ship 'raises her head and stern' at night, take soundings; if clear sky shows sun/moon/stars higher than horizon, heave to and sound; fixed mists/line/damp fog or flashes with little lights accompanied by thunder call for heaving to and sounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous natural signs indicate nearby land/rocks (greasy sea, leaves/branches, flocks of birds, patches of coloured water, different bird species' behavior); any of these cause an obligation to get soundings and be very careful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be especially vigilant for two principal dangers (land/rocks) but trust God ultimately
rubrics_metrics.description: While natural signs point to land or rocks and require vigilance, ultimate confidence is to be in God who alone knows and can guide and save ship and people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral/religious framing of practical vigilance; underscores humility and piety alongside navigational caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against natives' sabotage after anchoring
rubrics_metrics.description: After anchoring keep a careful lookout day and night because natives are good swimmers/divers and might wedge the rudder, cut hawsers, or set fire to the ship; in suspicious places have a guard in the boat at night over the buoys or visit them often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific defensive measures for ports where sabotage is plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and monitor native boarding to prevent being overpowered
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow so many natives on board as could overpower the crew; even few can cause evils from ignorance of our arms leading to war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care in admitting natives aboard; use hosts as needed but avoid risking crew safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landing procedures and caution (daytime landings only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect landings always by day, never at night; choose level, clear landing-places; send dogs ahead to discover ambushes, keep arms ready, march together and in order, enter passes with caution because natives may conceal themselves behind rocks, trees, or grass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes coordinated, armed, cautious approach; details on tactics (dogs, formation, scouting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detain chiefs as hostages when desirable but treat well and give presents
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible keep chiefs or important natives on the ship as hostages but well treated and given presents of things they like; similarly on shore give presents and conduct barter via one appointed person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostage-taking is tactical to secure cooperation; presents should be chosen to please and to imply value, facilitating barter and future relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade/barter conduct and intelligence gathering from natives
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct barter by one of our men who gives the natives to understand that our goods are of great value; learn whether there are other islands/lands, their colours, cannibalism, friendliness, gold/silver/pearls/spices/salt and where they are found, and write down native names for items and places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show pleasure at gifts, use signs to communicate, and have natives accompany parties when following up information to secure reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trust natives blindly; expect tricks and traps
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not follow natives' guidance except with great caution; never fully trust them whether they seem friendly or not because they may lead to pits or ambushes or deceive out of revenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When following native information, have the same natives accompany the party; do not mix with natives or allow free association that could endanger individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid eating native food and watch for poisoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not feed on things natives present to be eaten; do not fill hands or quit arms or take eyes off natives; watch for poison in food or water; only eat vegetables/fruits known before or seen eaten by birds/monkeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extreme caution regarding unknown foods; keep arms and vigilance while accepting any items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistreat natives or break pledges; avoid wanton destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Never ill-use or detain natives unless to return with clothes/presents; do not break peace or promises, nor cut down fruit trees, injure crops, or destroy houses/canoes, as this causes vengeance and withdrawal of food supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use demonstration of force only as warning (show arquebuses, swords) but refrain from actual destruction; maintain 'father to children' stance while watching them as potential enemies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical measures for embarking under attack
rubrics_metrics.description: If retreating to embark, have half the arquebusiers and shield-bearers face the natives to cover the other half embarking; those embarked must quickly turn to make same guard until all are embarked to guard against arrows, stones, darts, and lances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific formation and defensive choreography for safe embarkation under threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foraging parties to be well-armed and cautious; avoid unnecessary conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: When seeking wood, water, or provisions send a boat with well-armed men to overawe natives even where rupture seems unlikely; if opposition starts and need is not pressing return; if necessity is great, send a larger guard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer avoiding offensive actions; take measures to protect foragers and avoid provoking natives unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce cultivation and livestock on desert islands when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Sow profitable seeds (maize, beans, onions, cotton) on suitable islands; if possible land rabbits, goats, and swine to enrich desert lands for future navigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term provisioning and goodwill strategy for future ships and local supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and custody of goods upon sickness or death
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person falls sick, have him confess and make his will; if he dies, the master with a clerk should make an inventory of his goods and take charge to carry out wishes; if intestate, same inventory and care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical administrative procedure to ensure proper handling of deceased crew's effects and wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce supplies and ration water in emergency with oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: If supplies (notably water) run low, the Captain may reduce allowances (example: water consumption reduced from twelve/fifteen jars daily to three/four; Captain present when served and kept hatchway keys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captain must personally supervise rationing; innovations (e.g., distilling sea water) to augment supplies are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovate to produce freshwater when necessary (distillation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a brick oven and use a copper instrument to distil seawater to produce sweet water; invention provided several jars daily and could be improved to yield more with little fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical engineering solution noted as valuable; keep improving techniques to ensure adequate freshwater supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect careful observational signs of land from fauna and sea features
rubrics_metrics.description: Note bird types/behaviour (boobies vs. piqueros, assembly times), patches of coloured water (brown=rocks, white=sand, black=ooze, green=weeds), greasy sea, debris from rivers, flocks of fish and sea creatures as indicators of proximity and direction of land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiple signs (birds, sea colour, debris, currents, lightning behaviour) to assess proximity to land and take appropriate cautious actions (soundings, heave to).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult officers and record counsel when time-pressed
rubrics_metrics.description: If time is pressing and it appears necessary to exceed instructions, counsel should be taken with the Master, Pilot, officers, and other important persons; decisions should be signed with their names and done for service of God and the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective decision-making with signatures provides accountability for exceptions to orders.
